about.title: Fountain Valley Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Fountain Valley's mix of light industrial sites, retail centers, and businesses along corridors like Euclid and Brookhurst means workplace injuries show up in many forms — falls in a warehouse, forklift accidents, repetitive strain from assembly work, or injuries suffered by delivery drivers navigating I-405 access points. In California, workers' compensation is generally the only route against your employer, no matter who was at fault, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, a separate claim against that third party may be possible. Timing matters: you generally have 30 days to report the injury to your employer, and third-party claims carry a 2-year deadline. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect injured Fountain Valley workers with an independent attorney, free of charge, so you can understand which paths might apply to your situation before deadlines pass.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: When a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker contributed to your injury, workers' comp alone may not cover everything. An independent attorney can evaluate whether a separate third-party claim applies.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury. If you're worried about your job while considering a claim, an attorney can explain your protections.

items.title: Deadlines That Don't Wait
items.desc: Injuries must typically be reported to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims carry a 2-year statute of limitations. Missing either window can close off options, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt at work in Fountain Valley — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault. However, if a third party — like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim. An independent attorney can help sort out which applies to your case.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near I-405 or Brookhurst?
items.answer: Work-related driving injuries can involve both workers' compensation and a potential claim against another driver, especially given how much traffic moves through corridors like Brookhurst and I-405 during peak Friday evening hours. An independent attorney can look at the details and explain which claims might be available to you.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No — California law makes it illegal for employers to retaliate against workers for reporting an on-the-job injury. If you believe you've faced retaliation after reporting an injury, it's worth discussing your situation with an independent attorney who can explain your rights.
